nodes.label: Equity Block
nodes.rationale: Volunteer the tail metrics before anyone asks. p95 wait, worst wait and count waiting over five minutes would all worsen if the average were being bought by starving side streets.

nodes.label: Six-Month Corridor Pilot
nodes.rationale: Instrument one corridor. Diagonal has 184 segments and the signal hardware already exists, so this is a controller software change rather than a construction project.

nodes.label: Twin Clock Drift
nodes.rationale: The twins are separate OS processes stepping at different rates, so their clocks drift ~195s (~1%). The AI twin is normally ahead, so it has had longer to accumulate the emissions it is credited with reducing -- the live panel understates the case. Left uncorrected because a hand-applied factor cannot be audited.

nodes.label: Demand Drift Over Long Runs
nodes.rationale: Insertion slightly exceeds what the network clears, so vehicles accumulate and the advantage narrows from +38% at 0.5h to +16.5% at 4.2h. Restart before presenting.

nodes.label: Time-Integrated Speed
nodes.rationale: Total distance divided by total vehicle-seconds. The instantaneous mean is a single-tick sample of two independently seeded twins and swung +98% to -4% between consecutive samples while the underlying advantage sat steady.

nodes.label: Live Barcelona Traffic Feed
nodes.rationale: 532 instrumented sections, refreshed every few minutes, CC BY 4.0, no key. Three traps: only one of ~100 dataset resources is current, timestamps are Barcelona local with no offset marker, and state 0 means detector-down rather than clear.

nodes.label: Measured Result
nodes.rationale: Both twins run to t=1800s from 07:00. Speeds are time-integrated (distance / vehicle-seconds), not SUMO's instantaneous mean, because the volatile figure is the flattering one and does not reproduce.

nodes.label: Seed And Demand Validation
nodes.rationale: Re-runs the paired experiment four times varying both the SUMO driver-behaviour seed and the underlying trips, then reports the worst case across runs rather than the mean.

nodes.label: Bounded By Construction
nodes.rationale: Only eight named anchors and three corridors exist, so the model cannot invent coordinates that would land outside the network and silently inject nothing. Counts clamp at 5,000 per event, max 4 events.

nodes.label: Emissions Warm-Up Artefact
nodes.rationale: For the first ten simulated minutes CO2 reads WORSE for the AI, because it completed 141 trips to the baseline's 63 and so burned more fuel doing more than twice the work. Delay and bus rows are meaningful from minute one; emissions are not.

nodes.label: The Honest Claim
nodes.rationale: Streets and signals are real; trips are modelled because Barcelona publishes no O/D matrix. The claim is that the RELATIVE improvement between two identical cities is real.

nodes.label: Teleports Understate The Result
nodes.rationale: SUMO teleports vehicles deadlocked for four minutes. Fixed-time triggers it about twice as often as the AI, and teleported vehicles stop accruing delay, so the measured gap is smaller than the real one.

nodes.label: Twin Experiment
nodes.rationale: Two identical cities run the same streets, trips and RNG seed; the only difference is the signal controller. Modelled demand cancels out of the comparison, which is why the experiment is a twin rather than a single before/after run.

nodes.label: Worst-Case Reporting
nodes.rationale: Quote the least favourable figure across validation runs, not the mean. The number you should be willing to defend is the worst one.

nodes.label: Congestion Is Not Volume
nodes.rationale: The trams feed reports how congested a section IS, not how many vehicles are on it. An empty road at 03:00 still reports 'very fluid', so the measured index floors at ~0.45 of peak while real volume is nearer 0.10. The demand curve's SHAPE is measured and its AMPLITUDE rescaled.

nodes.label: No Default Endpoint
nodes.rationale: A plausible-looking URL invented in source would be a fabricated data source that appears to work. Optional feeds stay inert until both a key and a URL are supplied.

nodes.label: Model Chooses, Simulation Decides
nodes.rationale: The emulator translates intent into bounded parameters but does not invent traffic physics. An LLM guessing at congestion outcomes would be fabrication; an LLM writing a plausible incident and handing it to a validated simulator is a better input device.

nodes.label: Policy Reaches The AI Twin Only
nodes.norm_label: policy reaches the ai twin only
nodes.rationale: Sending policy to the baseline would destroy the A/B the entire demo rests on. Scenario EVENTS by contrast go to both twins identically, for the same reason.

nodes.label: Two Keys, Not One
nodes.rationale: The emulator invents traffic; the orchestrator influences signal timing. Different trust levels get different credentials, so they can be budgeted, rate-limited, revoked and audited independently, and a compromised scenario generator has no path to the control loop.

nodes.label: Rules Over Reinforcement Learning
nodes.rationale: A transport authority has to sign it off. Every decision is explainable in one sentence and failure modes are bounded by construction. RL is phase two, once the pilot has generated field data to train on.

nodes.label: Policy Bounds Clamped Twice
nodes.rationale: Bounds are applied after parsing the response and again in apply_policy. The duplication is deliberate: this is the last line before parameters reach 1,151 live controllers, and a bound that only exists in the caller disappears the first time someone adds a second caller.

nodes.label: Strategic / Tactical Split
nodes.rationale: An LLM cannot drive 1,151 junctions at 1 Hz -- roughly 69,000 sub-second decisions a minute. The strategic layer sets five policy parameters every ~60 simulated seconds; the tactical layer runs six auditable rules at 1 Hz. The layer that can be wrong in surprising ways never touches a signal directly.

nodes.label: Dead Reckoning
nodes.rationale: The wire carries no vehicle IDs, so vehicles cannot be matched frame-to-frame and cannot be interpolated. Each advances along its reported heading at its reported speed until the next tick corrects it.

nodes.label: Binary Wire Format
nodes.rationale: One binary frame per tick: header JSON, then float32 per vehicle, then one byte per signal approach and per edge. JSON would be ~8x larger for the vehicle array and would stall the main thread on parse.

nodes.label: Instance Slot Instability
nodes.rationale: The vehicle array is repacked every tick and a slot holds the same vehicle only 36.4% of the time. Easing yaw from the slot's previous heading rendered a rotation more than 15 degrees wrong on 55.2% of slot-ticks. Turn rate therefore travels per-vehicle on the wire.

nodes.label: Web App Shell
nodes.rationale: Minimal dark-scheme shell mounting a single React root from src/main.jsx.

nodes.label: Building Coverage Trade-Off
nodes.rationale: The 3D city covers 17% of the simulated footprint. Judged on the target machine rather than the download: the file is served from localhost, so the cost is parse time and GPU load for ~30k extruded polygons on an Intel N100.

nodes.label: Model Fallback Chains
nodes.rationale: Not defensive over-engineering: building it hit model-retired (404), model-at-capacity (503) and model-unreachable inside an hour on live endpoints. On the first live scenario call the configured model 503'd and the chain fell through.

nodes.label: Failure Is A Non-Event
nodes.rationale: Any error returns the previous policy unchanged and records the reason. A signal network must not change behaviour because an HTTP call failed. The decision runs on its own thread so a slow call never stalls the simulation.

nodes.label: Pedestrian Demand Gap
nodes.rationale: Pedestrians are not modelled as crossing demand -- the acknowledged gap. Pedestrian phases are baked into imported signal programs and minimum green is never violated, so crossing time is preserved.
